tooltip.more_quad: Right-click: quadrupole treatment (first order, fixed or powder Kündig, Hamiltonian, single crystal).
tooltip.fixed_cb: Ticked: the parameter is NOT fitted; it stays at its value.
tooltip.p_delta: Isomer shift (mm/s), referred to α-Fe. Moves the whole subspectrum.
tooltip.p_quad: Quadrupole splitting (mm/s). In a sextet it shifts lines 1,6 against 2-5.
tooltip.p_bhf: Magnetic hyperfine field (T). Sets the separation of the six sextet lines.
tooltip.p_gamma1: Full width at half maximum (mm/s) of the outer lines 1,6. This is the reference width.
tooltip.p_gamma2: Width of lines 2,5 relative to Γ1. It is 1 when every line has the same width.
tooltip.p_gamma3: Width of lines 3,4 relative to Γ1. It is 1 when every line has the same width.
tooltip.p_depth: Absorption depth of the reference line, as a fraction of the baseline.
tooltip.p_int1: Intensity of lines 1,6 relative to 3,4. In a random powder it is 3.
tooltip.p_int2: Intensity of lines 2,5 relative to 3,4. Orientation-dependent: 2 in a random powder, 0 to 4 with texture.
tooltip.p_texture: Texture angle (degrees) between the beam and the magnetic moment. It sets the 1,6 and 2,5 intensities.
tooltip.p_beta: Angle β (degrees) between the magnetic field and the principal axis of the electric field gradient.
tooltip.p_eta: Asymmetry parameter of the electric field gradient, from 0 (axial) to 1. Hamiltonian treatment only.
tooltip.p_phi: Azimuthal angle φ (degrees) of the magnetic field in the electric field gradient frame.
tooltip.p_bex: Polar angle of the γ beam with respect to the principal axis of the gradient. Single crystal only.
tooltip.p_gax: Azimuthal angle of the γ beam in the gradient frame. Single crystal only.
tooltip.p_relax_fraction: Fraction of the subspectrum that relaxes, from 0 (all blocked) to 1 (all relaxing).
tooltip.p_relax_log_nu: Base-10 logarithm of the jump frequency (Hz). The higher it is, the more collapsed the sextet.
tooltip.p_relax_polarization: Imbalance between the populations of the two states, from −1 to +1. At 0 both are equally likely.
tooltip.p_neel_temp_k: Measurement temperature (K). It enters the Néel-Arrhenius law.
tooltip.p_neel_log10_keff: Base-10 logarithm of the effective anisotropy (J/m³). With the volume it sets the energy barrier.
tooltip.p_neel_mean_d_nm: Mean particle diameter (nm) of the lognormal distribution.
tooltip.p_neel_sigma: Width of the lognormal size distribution. 0 would mean a single size.
tooltip.p_neel_log10_tau0: Base-10 logarithm of the attempt time τ₀ (s). Usually between −13 and −9.
tooltip.p_neel_bins: Number of sizes the distribution is discretised into. More gives finer detail and more computation.
tooltip.c_vmax: Maximum transducer velocity (mm/s). It sets the axis scale and comes from the α-Fe calibration.
tooltip.c_center: Channel at which the spectrum is folded. If the residual is antisymmetric around the lines, check this before the model.
tooltip.c_baseline: Baseline level, in normalised counts. 1 is transmission with no absorption.
tooltip.c_slope: Linear slope of the baseline with velocity. It absorbs the spectrometer drift.
tooltip.c_curv: Quadratic baseline term (v²). Useful when the geometry leaves curvature after folding.
tooltip.c_curv3: Cubic baseline term (v³). Equivalent to NORMOS BKG(4); rarely needed.
tooltip.c_curv4: Quartic baseline term (v⁴). Equivalent to NORMOS BKG(5); rarely needed.
tooltip.c_voigt_sigma: Gaussian width σ (mm/s) of the Voigt profile. It absorbs instrumental broadening or mild disorder.
tooltip.c_sat_scale: Saturation scale of the thick absorber. It corrects deep lines no longer growing with thickness.
tooltip.c_src_fwhm: Full width at half maximum of the source line (mm/s). It is convolved with the absorber.
tooltip.c_line_profile: Lorentzian: the natural line shape. Voigt: adds a Gaussian width σ for instrumental broadening or mild disorder.
tooltip.more_help: Right-click ▸ More information: opens the help chapter that explains this parameter.

conventions.sextet_tip: NORMOS derives the line positions from the nuclear moments; on the same spectrum the field differs by ~0.01 T at 33 T.
conventions.intensity_tip: They only differ when the widths Γ2/Γ3 are not equal to Γ1.
conventions.relax_tip: They only differ for polarization P > 0; the NORMOS one does not satisfy detailed balance.
bhf.field_advanced_tip: Unchecked, each P(ΔEQ) column is a doublet (B = 0), the usual case. Check it only to distribute the quadrupole shift of a sextet at a fixed field.
bhf.warn_thin_absorber: ⚠ Distribution fits assume a thin absorber: the «Absorber» setting is not applied here.
bhf.warn_is_gamma: ⚠ An IS distribution broadens all lines equally and trades off against Γ: fix Γ («Fixed» box) for P(IS) to be meaningful.
bhf.warn_quad_gamma: ⚠ With doublets, P(ΔEQ) broadens both lines just like Γ and the two trade off: fix Γ («Fixed» box) for the width of P(ΔEQ) to be reliable.
bhf.warn_quad_field: ⚠ With B ≠ 0 each column is a first-order sextet: valid only if ΔEQ is much smaller than the magnetic splitting (not suitable for applied fields of a few tesla).
bhf.warn_is_quad_2d: ⚠ With doublets only the distribution of each line (δ ± ΔEQ/2) is observed: the IS–ΔEQ map is not unique (σ IS, σ ΔEQ and ρ trade off). For the IS–ΔEQ correlation use P(ΔEQ) with κδ.
batch.no_numeric_data: There is no numeric data to plot.
bhf.lcurve_only_distribution: Only available in P(BHF) / P(ΔEQ) distribution mode.

rep.title: Fit report
rep.dist_no_sigma: Without the data σ, χ², AIC and BIC are not computed.
rep.dist_aic_note: AIC and BIC use the same definition as the discrete fit: they can be compared with a discrete fit of the same spectrum (lower is better).
rep.dist_band_note: Monte Carlo 1σ band (100 refits): plot and exported data
rep.dist_edge_pileup: P piles up weight at the edge of the grid ({pct} % of the maximum): the distribution extends beyond the grid; widen it.
rep.no_dist_result: Distribution mode without a fit: fit the distribution before exporting the report.
rep.gl_p_note: Weight of each value of the variable on the grid, normalised to unit area (binomial: P_k summing to 1).
rep.gl_alpha_note: Weight of smoothness against fit in the histogram; dimensionless, log α ≈ 0 is the natural balance.
rep.gl_kappa_note: Linear variation of δ or ΔEQ with the grid variable, from its value at the centre of the grid.
rep.gl_k_note: k = effective degrees of the distribution (trace of the regularised operator, or the number of parameters of a shape) + refined globals; ν = N − k.
rep.fit_vmax: Fit Vmax with the line pattern
rep.no_calib: No active calibration; δ values are not corrected.
rep.resid_warning: The residual seems to have non-random structure. Check the model, the *folding point*, the Vmax calibration or whether components are missing.
rep.corr_matrix_note: Rows and columns are the parameters (columns numbered like the rows). r > 0: they move together; r < 0: in opposite directions. |r| ≥ 0.8: they partly trade off; bold, |r| ≥ 0.95: the fit cannot separate them.
rep.texture_header: Quantities derived from the texture (t = sin²θ)
rep.texture_note: *t = sin²θ* parametrises the I₂/I₃ intensity ratio of the sextet: t = 0 ⇒ field parallel to the γ ray (I₂ = 0), t = 2/3 ⇒ random sample (θ ≈ 54.7°, R₂₃ = 2), t = 1 ⇒ perpendicular field (R₂₃ = 4). *S* is a Hermans-type order parameter: **+1** aligned with γ, **0** isotropic, **−½** perpendicular.
rep.gl_delta_note: Electron charge density at the nucleus; relative to α-Fe.
rep.gl_quad_note: Asymmetry of the electric field gradient at the nucleus.
rep.gl_bhf_note: Local magnetism felt by the nucleus.
rep.gl_gamma_note: Full width at half maximum of the line profile.
rep.gl_depth_note: Relative amplitude of the component; related to the Mössbauer effect and the thickness.
rep.gl_int_note: Nominal ratios 3 : I₂ : 1 for a sextet.
rep.gl_texture_note: t = sin²θ with θ = angle of the field to γ; controls I₂/I₃.
rep.gl_beta_note: Only with the fixed Kündig quadrupole treatment.
rep.gl_voigt: Gaussian σ of the Voigt profile
rep.gl_baseline_note: Level and slope of the transmission background.
plimit.is_lo: IS min  (outer δ-axis bound in IS mode)
plimit.is_hi: IS max  (outer δ-axis bound in IS mode)
plimit.quad_lo: ΔEQ min  (outer bound of distributed ΔEQ axis)
plimit.quad_hi: ΔEQ max  (outer bound of distributed ΔEQ axis)
plimit.lcurve_alpha_lo: L-curve: log₁₀ α min of the scan

normos.w_bhf_scale: BHF is on the NORMOS scale (positions derived from the nuclear moments). To reproduce it, fit with core.constants.sextet_pattern("normos").
normos.w_pfp_seed: PFP={pfp} is the SEED of the folding-point search, not the final value: NORMOS refines it over two cycles and quantises it to multiples of half a channel. It is not imposed — Fitbauer runs its own search. To force it, type it by hand into "Center".
normos.w_n_blocks: the job has {n} distribution blocks (NSB(2..)>0); Fitbauer handles only one: block 1 is imported.
normos.w_method_unknown: Unknown METHOD={method}; a BHF distribution is assumed.
normos.w_method2: METHOD=2 (Brand-style first-order asymmetry): Fitbauer models that asymmetry with the δ(H) correlation, already carried over from DTI, but not with Brand's full expansion.
normos.w_method3: METHOD=3 (Billard & Chamberod sum over neighbours) is not in Fitbauer: it is imported as a simple distribution with the same δ(H)/ΔEQ(H) correlations.
normos.w_method_file: METHOD={method} reads the distribution from an external file; in Fitbauer that is the "Fixed" shape: load the file by hand.
normos.w_distri4: DISTRI=4 (Czjzek if METHOD=6, Le Caer if METHOD=7) is imported as a histogram: Fitbauer has the Czjzek and extended Czjzek shapes, but they have not been checked to use the same parametrisation as NORMOS; choose them by hand in the panel.
normos.w_step: {name} is not positive: NORMOS uses 1.0 by default and so does Fitbauer, but check the grid range.
normos.w_dtq_ignored: DTQ={dtq} appears in the .JOB but NORMOS IGNORES it in field distributions (METHOD 1-5): only DTI modulates the subspectrum. It is not carried over.
normos.w_is_field: BHF={bhf} with METHOD=8: Fitbauer's P(IS) always uses B = 0; it is imported without a field.
normos.w_sti: STI/STG (Gaussian width of the isomer shift) is not carried over; in Fitbauer the equivalent route is the Voigt profile.
normos.w_lamda: LAMDA={lamda} is not carried over as is: Fitbauer's α is dimensionless (normalised by λ_ref) and NORMOS's is absolute. Use the L-curve to set it.
normos.w_beta12: BETA1={b1} and BETA2={b2} anchor the two grid ends with different weights; Fitbauer uses a single edge_anchor and takes the larger one ({anchor} relative to λ).
normos.w_beta_gui: BETA1/BETA2 anchor the grid ends (β/λ = {anchor}). The GUI panel does not expose that control: if you need it, pass it as "edge_anchor" to fit_hyperfine_distribution.
normos.w_dist_ignored: NORMOS-DIST IGNORES these .JOB keys (they are not in its &PARAM namelist): {keys}. If they came from a SITE job, that subspectrum never entered the fit.
normos.w_bkg: {name} = {value}: the NORMOS polynomial background is normalised to (v/Δv)^k; check "{target}" after importing.
normos.w_octet: subspectrum {i}: octet (NLINE=8) imported as a sextet; lines 7,8 (ΔmI=±2) must be added as singlets.
normos.w_ndex_out: constraint NDEX({target})={source}: index outside the imported model; skipped.
normos.w_area_link: area constraint NDEX({target})={source} rescaled to depths with the JOB widths; if the fit changes the widths, check the area ratio.
normos.w_key_not_carried: "{name}" is not carried over: check the model by hand.
normos.w_binomial_nsb: Binomial with NSB={nsb}: NORMOS uses 13 subspectra (0–12 neighbours) and with NSB≠13 truncates or pads with meaningless weights; Fitbauer always uses all 13.
normos.w_nxll_spline: crystalline site {i}: NXLL={nxll} points to a spline spectrum in a file; not imported.
normos.w_nxll: crystalline site {i}: NXLL={nxll} not supported; skipped.
normos.e_dist_job: this is a NORMOS-DIST job (distributions), not NORMOS-SITE: its NSUB are the points of the distribution grid, not discrete sites. Set up the distribution from the Fitbauer panel.

bhf.vbf_sigma_order: σ max ({max}) must be greater than σ min ({min})
tooltip.show_correlation: The δ(x) or ΔEQ(x) line the kernel applied with the κ slopes, with its 1σ band if they were refined. Solid where the distribution has weight; dotted elsewhere, where it is an extrapolation.
tooltip.show_prob_band: 1σ uncertainty of each bin of P from a parametric Monte Carlo: the distribution is refitted on the model plus noise of the data σ (scaled by the reduced χ²) and the spread is measured. It respects P ≥ 0. It does not include the uncertainty of δ, Γ or the other global values. Histogram shape with Tikhonov or TV only.
